result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.count_nonisomorphic_trees()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Count the trees on order nodes up to isomorphism. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.count_nonisomorphic_trees()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Count the trees on order nodes up to isomorphism. title: >- [Graph.count_nonisomorphic_trees()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Count the trees on order nodes up to isomorphism. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count the trees on `order` nodes up to isomorphism. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16034-L16083){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.count_nonisomorphic_trees(order) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Count non-isomorphic trees](../assets/graphs/count-nonisomorphic-trees.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: the three trees on five nodes, the path, the chair, and the star, each drawn with its longest path as a row and any other nodes hanging below. Right: a table of how many trees there are on 3 to 9 nodes, 1, 2, 3, 6, 11, 23, and 47, with the count 3 for five nodes highlighted. The count comes from a formula, without building the trees, and roughly doubles with each added node at these sizes." width="100%"} Returns the number of unlabeled (free) trees on `order` nodes, the number of graphs `iter_nonisomorphic_trees()` yields, without building them: 1, 1, 2, 3, 6, 11, 23, 47, 106, 235, ... for 2, 3, 4, ... nodes (OEIS A000055). It uses Otter's formula, which expresses free trees through rooted ones, whose numbers follow a recurrence over divisors, as NetworkX's `number_of_nonisomorphic_trees()` does. The result is an exact Python integer however large it gets. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [order]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. Must be at least `2`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The number of non-isomorphic trees on `order` nodes. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `order=` is less than `2`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The counts grow roughly threefold with each node: ::: {#01c64ac6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec [ec.Graph.count_nonisomorphic_trees(n) for n in range(2, 13)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 1, 2, 3, 6, 11, 23, 47, 106, 235, 551] ``` ::: ::: Counting is fast even where listing would be hopeless: ::: {#ea124141 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph.count_nonisomorphic_trees(100) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 630134658347465720563607281977639527019590 ``` ::: :::
